The Type Atlas

formex-type-atlas.Rmd

This article is a field guide to the data types formex knows: for each one, a worked example, the signal its detector keys off, what it hands back to a consumer such as datagoodr, and an honest rating of how hard it is to detect, stabilize, and round-trip through a CSV. For implementation status and coverage gaps, see the companion DEVELOPMENT-STATUS.md note at the repository root.

All counts below are computed live from the shipped ontology, so they track the package rather than this prose.

o <- fx_ontology()
c(variants = nrow(o),
  families = length(unique(paste(o$data_type, o$semantic_family))),
  implemented = sum(o$implemented == "yes"))
#>    variants    families implemented 
#>          97          25          48

The organizing idea: six detection mechanisms

Every variant carries a match_kind — how its detector decides. It is the single best predictor of accuracy and of whether stabilization is reliable.

table(o$match_kind)
#> 
#>       genome      lexicon         mask mask+lexicon         none        shape 
#>            3           11           49            7           15           12
match_kind confirm* how it decides
genome ~0.97 Full parse. Tries a library of date/time formats built from a format “genome”; a value matches only if some format parses it to a valid, in-range value and round-trips.
shape ~0.81 Numeric value profile — range, sign, decimals. Recognizes “a number” but not which numeric subtype.
mask ~0.72 Positional character-class / regex mask (9(2)-9(7)); some add a checksum (EIN, DEA) or a fixed length + alphabet (hashes).
lexicon ~0.64 Membership in a curated reference list — given names, surnames, US cities, ISO-3166, USPS. Coverage-limited.
mask+lexicon ~0.25 Shape and a reference lookup — postal addresses, FIPS keys. The hardest combinations.
none n/a Not value-detectable by construction. The role lives in the header or codebook, not the values.

* “confirm” is the per-mechanism recipe reliability given a correct label — confirm_if_true from the dev/stabilize_rate.R harness: the share of correctly-labeled columns whose recipe normalizes and validates to a non-NA stable value. It is a column-level yield, not a detection-accuracy or a per-variant figure.

Failure is graceful everywhere

The verifier is foil-selective: each candidate recipe must confirm the column and reject a fixed junk foil. A permissive recipe (a numeric coerce, a free-text as_factor) that also accepts the foil cannot claim a leaf, so the column truncates to the deepest path it can defend (depth 0–4) with lower confidence instead of forcing a false guess.

# a clean date resolves all the way to a leaf (depth 4)
guess_data_type(c("03/15/2019", "12/31/2020"))$route$depth
#> [1] 4
# a bare integer column cannot defend a leaf and truncates
guess_data_type(c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5"))$route$depth
#> [1] 3

What crosses the wire to a consumer

formex is stateless and answers one column at a time; datagoodr orchestrates and holds the governance state. They meet only at the ontology’s stable keys, semantic_type_id and variant_id.

 1. PROFILE    fx_extract_features(col)                     [formex]
 2. CLASSIFY   guess_data_type(col, name)  router→verifier  [formex]
 3. GOVERN     append governance row; auto-accept or flag   [datagoodr]
 4. STABILIZE  fx_stabilize(col, type, label)               [formex]
 5. EMIT       cleaned dataset + import-rule sidecar         [datagoodr]

Classification (2) is probabilistic; transformation (4) is a pure function of the confirmed recipe. A human override in step 3 changes which recipe step 4 runs, nothing else.

The functions a consumer calls

function needs returns
guess_data_type(x, name) column values x; optional header name (a tiebreak / for metadata-gated classes) legacy $guess/$ontology/$confidence plus a $route record. Values-first: a real value signature always wins over the name
fx_stabilize(x, semantic_type, format_label) raw values and the confirmed (semantic_type, format_label) — i.e. the variant_id written into the governance file variant_id, format_mask, stable (normalized values), stable_format, import_rule
fx_extract_features(x, col_name) the column values; optional name the ~477-number value profile the learned router consumes
as_mm(), as_EIN(), autotype helpers values to coerce / test cases to build format-coerced vectors and detector benchmark fixtures

The export record: $route

This is the object that lands in the governance file as the guess_* fields. A human then confirms or overrides final_variant_id, the only thing that steers fx_stabilize.

str(guess_data_type(c("03/15/2019", "12/31/2020", "01/01/2021"))$route[
  c("data_type", "semantic_family", "semantic_type", "format_label",
    "variant_id", "match_kind", "depth", "confidence", "dd_unit")])
#> List of 9
#>  $ data_type      : chr "temporal"
#>  $ semantic_family: chr "date"
#>  $ semantic_type  : chr "calendar"
#>  $ format_label   : chr "calendar"
#>  $ variant_id     : chr "n0059-f01"
#>  $ match_kind     : chr "genome"
#>  $ depth          : int 4
#>  $ confidence     : num 1
#>  $ dd_unit        : chr NA

depth is 0 unknown · 1 data_type · 2 family · 3 semantic_type · 4 leaf. dd_unit is metadata the row declares (e.g. a currency), never a value prediction — units are not value-detectable in general (100 could be lb or kg).

Every family, rated

Green is favorable, amber is caution, red is a known hard spot, grey is a neutral fact — nuance is not a defect. Desired form asks whether the final analysis-ready version is one predictable shape (uniform) or has several valid presentations, units, or encodings (nuanced).

family mechanism detect accuracy stabilize CSV round-trip* desired form
date temporal genome easy excellent straightforward yes · ISO uniform
time temporal genome easy excellent straightforward yes · ISO uniform
period temporal mask medium good straightforward yes mostly uniform (fiscal vs. calendar)
phase temporal lexicon/mask medium mixed moderate label lost (stores numeric position) nuanced
interval temporal mask medium good splits column needs rule (→ _start/_end) nuanced
id identifier mask / mask+lex med–high scheme-dependent (hash/UUID high, surrogate low) moderate needs rule (leading zeros · as_id) uniform per scheme
contact text mask low–med high (email/phone) high yes email uniform, phone nuanced
web text mask low–med good moderate yes mostly uniform
color text mask low high hex only (rgb/hsl/cmyk pass through) yes uniform per space
name text lexicon hard low–med (gazetteer-limited) pass-through yes nuanced
postal text mask+lex hard low · 0.25 pass-through yes nuanced
text (free) text none hard (residual) low pass-through yes uniform · preserve
quantity number shape hard (subtype not value-visible) low low class undetermined nuanced · units vary
currency number mask medium straightforward straightforward unit lost (→ dd_unit) nuanced
portion number shape low moderate (needs class) yes nuanced (0–1 vs 0–100)
range number mask medium splits column needs rule (→ _lo/_hi) nuanced
coordinate number mask med–high moderate (splits · CRS) needs rule nuanced (order · CRS)
mutually exclusive categorical lex / none mixed (geo/NAICS yes, nominal no) mixed needs levels needs codebook nuanced
scale categorical none hard low needs levels needs codebook nuanced
multiselect categorical none hard low splits to list needs rule nuanced
binary boolean mask medium (loose · 0/1 ≈ numeric) medium straightforward (→ TRUE/FALSE) encoding map uniform output, inputs vary
collection structured mask low–med pass-through opaque as text yes · text nuanced
record structured mask low–med pass-through opaque as text yes · text nuanced
geometry structured mask medium pass-through opaque as text yes · WKT nuanced
unknown unknown none — residual graceful floor none · retain yes · text uniform · preserve

* “CSV round-trip without rules” — whether the stable value reads back correctly from a plain CSV with no import rule. The classic failure is an identifier: write 06037 and a spreadsheet reads it as the number 6037. The import_rule the engine returns (as_id, as_factor with levels, …) is what makes the file self-describing.

By data type

For each type: a representative example, what the detector reads, what trips it up, and the stable value + import rule that go back to the consumer. The fx_stabilize() output below is live.

Temporal — the strong corner (genome) 

fx_stabilize(c("03/15/2019", "3-15-2019"), "calendar")[c("stable", "import_rule")]
#> $stable
#> [1] "2019-03-15" "2019-03-15"
#> 
#> $import_rule
#> [1] "{{ as_yyyymmdd }}"

Keys off: not one regex per shape — a library of formats built from the date genome (component order × month form × delimiter). A value is a date only if some format parses it to a valid in-range date and the parse round-trips. Trips it up: ambiguous mm/dd vs dd/mm; two-digit years; a bare four-digit year is excluded on purpose (indistinguishable from a count or ID).

Identifier — strong patterns, but the CSV hazard 

fx_stabilize(c("6037", "06037"), "geographic", "county_fips")[c("stable", "import_rule")]
#> $stable
#> [1] NA      "06037"
#> 
#> $import_rule
#> [1] "{{ as_factor }}"

Keys off: positional masks, sharpened where possible — EIN/DEA/Chinese-ID validate a check digit; hashes by fixed length + hex alphabet (MD5 32, SHA-1 40, SHA-256 64); FIPS by a lexicon anchored on a valid 2-digit state prefix. Trips it up: surrogate/record keys are value-undetectable (a bare integer key looks like a count — stays ~0% by design); leading-zero loss on import.

Text — strong on contact/web, limited on names 

rbind(
  email = fx_stabilize("Jane@Example.ORG", "email")["stable"],
  phone = fx_stabilize("(605) 348-9999", "phone")["stable"])
#>       stable            
#> email "jane@example.org"
#> phone "6053489999"

Keys off: masks for email/phone/URL/IP/MAC/color (clear patterns); lexicons for person and place names. Free text, labels and titles are none — a residual, not a signature. Trips it up: names outside the gazetteer are invisible; organizations are an open set with no closed recipe.

Number — the detection ceiling (shape) 

fx_stabilize(c("$2300.00", "17,298$", "$-45"), "usd")[c("stable", "import_rule")]
#> $stable
#> [1] "2300"  "17298" "-45"  
#> 
#> $import_rule
#> [1] "{{ default:numeric }}"

Keys off: plain quantities/portions are shape — a numeric profile that says “a number” but not which subtype. Currency/range/coordinate add a mask. Trips it up: the core limit of the engine — 100 could be a count, score, index, or lb/kg; 0.05 a probability, rate, or ratio. These route shallow and wait for the header. Note usd strips the symbol and grouping to a bare number; the currency itself rides along as dd_unit, carried not predicted.

Categorical — only closed sets confirm by value 

fx_stabilize(c("California", "TX", "Ohio"), "geographic", "us_state")[c("stable", "import_rule")]
#> $stable
#> [1] "CA" "TX" "OH"
#> 
#> $import_rule
#> [1] "{{ as_factor }}"

Keys off: only closed-set members confirm by value — geography (USPS/FIPS) and classification codes (NAICS). Nominal, ordinal, Likert and rating scales are none: the category role is a header/codebook fact. Trips it up: codes look like IDs or small integers; ordering and level labels cannot be recovered from values, so a factor needs its declared level set to read back from a CSV.

Boolean, structured, unknown

Boolean keys off a small two-state vocabulary (1/0, y/n, t/f, checkbox); is_boolean() is marked loose because 0/1 overlaps numeric codes, and the boolean class (indicator vs. presence vs. status vs. response) needs the name. Structured keys off serialization syntax (JSON, key-value, WKT/WKB/GeoJSON) and is preserved as a literal — it round-trips as text but stays opaque to the frame. Unknown is the explicit resting place for graceful truncation: retain the source text, log parse errors, do not coerce.
